title: ATP Ventures unveiled, men’s top tour significantly increasing prize money
article_text:
The board of men's tennis' top-tier ATP has given the green light to launch ATP Ventures, a new vehicle set to manage the body's commercial and media rights.

This comes as part of a wider sweep of changes to the structure of men's top-tier tennis that will also see the total prize money available to players increase to over $350 million by 2028. That figure is currently set at $270 million.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

It also forms the latest chapter in OneVision, the long-term campaign to increase the ATP's revenue and commercial appeal that began in 2023 (having been in development since 2020).

The creation of ATP Ventures will bring all of the media and sponsorship rights for the ATP Tour under one roof for the first time.

It comes with plans to create a joint commercial venture between the ATP and women's tennis' WTA, which had fallen through earlier this year.

The launch of this new vehicle has been unanimously approved by the ATP's board, alongside the shareholders of the ATP Media wing.

It comes as the end-of-year ATP Finals take place currently in Turin, Italy.

The rights combined will cover those held by the ATP Tour itself, ATP Media, as well as those held by the Tennis Data Innovations vehicle.

The Florida-based ATP has said that work on the agreement will begin next year, and that the venture will become operational from the start of 2028.

Andrea Gaudenzi, chair of the ATP, commented: "The next phase of OneVision strengthens our product, while ATP Ventures will transform how we take it to market. Bringing ATP Media, TDI and our central sponsorship business together under one aligned commercial strategy gives us a huge opportunity to grow the Tour, tell a stronger story around our players and bring fans closer to the sport.”

Regarding the financial element of this news, the increased player prize money will include an increase in the bonus pool figure to $50 million, a bonus of $25 million covering end-of-year rankings, and $26 million in player pension funding.

As a contrast, the 2026 bonus pool for ATP professionals only comes to $21 million.

The ATP Tour announced earlier this month that central partnership revenues had increased 49% year-on-year in 2026, to more than $100 million, for the first time.

This came on the back of new agreements and expanded investments from long-standing partners including flag carrier airline Emirates, tech company Infosys, parts manufacturer Nitto, luxury carmaker Lexus, home appliances corporation Haier, and tyre manufacturer Yokohama.

Overall, OneVision represents the organization's long-term strategic plan to reform professional tennis, align interests between players and tournaments, and grow the sport’s commercial digital footprint.

Earlier this year, the tour re-elected Gaudenzi as chairman for a third term until 2028, meanwhile.

Recent growth has also been driven by the launch of the ATP’s dedicated Licensing and Retail team within its central business division in 2025, which has opened the door to new licensing agreements, including K-Swiss’ agreement to create a collection of five ATP-branded tennis shoes.

title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
article_text:
Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Las Vegas GP pole by 0.073s to Max Verstappen despite ideal track position

For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds.

The result stung after Russell had looked untouchable earlier in the evening, topping final practice with a 1m34.041s that put him 0.911s clear of Antonelli. Complicating matters in Q3, Russell had asked Mercedes for a slipstream from his already-penalised team-mate.

Instead, a messy final out-lap left Antonelli trailing the pack, allowing the Italian to pull a tow worth up to 16 km/h down the Strip straight from cars ahead—including Russell.

Asked after qualifying whether Mercedes should have orchestrated a better tow to aid Russell’s fight for second in the Drivers’ Championship, Wolff dismissed track positioning as the culprit.

"Actually, George for me had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said. "We need to find out because I think there was some kind of Turn 7, 8, 9 - whether there was a mistake or something else happened, I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time."

Even without pole, Russell lines up second alongside Verstappen on Saturday night with major championship stakes on the line. Sitting third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, Russell has a prime chance to make serious ground after both Ferraris - Charles Leclerc (11th) and Lewis Hamilton (12th) - were knocked out in Q2.

Tension between the front-row rivals is already running hot. Late in FP3, Verstappen and Russell tangled wheel-to-wheel at Turn 14 after Verstappen passed the Mercedes and slowed into the corner, prompting the Dutchman to complain over team radio that Russell had "pushed me into the barrier". Following a post-session review, the FIA stewards handed Verstappen a warning for the skirmish.

Asked what he expected when the pair launch side by side toward Turn 1, Wolff didn't downplay the prospect of fireworks.

"Well, with cinema, if they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching," Wolff said.

title: Frontier Airlines & BarkleyOKRP ink the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship
article_text:
November, 2026.- Most airlines launch premium seats with typical luxury marketing and visuals. Not Frontier Airlines. They decided to pen the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship, literally sponsoring the actual rear ends of college football’s heaviest players.

Frontier and BarkleyOKRP partnered with two #2-ranked University of Georgia offensive linemen, Jahzare Jackson (6’10”, 350 lbs) and Juan Gaston (6’7”, 360 lbs), for what they’re calling the world’s “biggest” NIL deal. And they took the signing quite literally. The 710-pound duo made their endorsements official by dipping their backsides in paint and stamping their contracts with their butts.

The campaign comes as Frontier works to reshape perceptions of the airline, introducing a series of cabin enhancements that include First Class seating, more extra-legroom options, in-seat power and Starlink Wi-Fi. Rather than relying on traditional premium airline advertising, BarkleyOKRP turned an NIL partnership into an unexpected demonstration of one of those upgrades: If Frontier’s new First Class seats can comfortably accommodate two SEC offensive linemen, they can accommodate just about anyone.

The campaign launches November 18 across social and digital channels, bringing an unexpected twist to both airline advertising and the increasingly crowded world of NIL deals.

title: SA top sprinter Akani Simbine joins forces with Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold road race
article_text:
Sibanye-Stillwater and the Simbine Classic have announced a three-year sponsorship that will introduce the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 5km and 10km road races at the 2027 World Athletics Continental Tour event, providing recreational runners and walkers with the opportunity to participate in one of the country’s premier athletics showcases.

The MyGold races will make their debut in Pretoria on 17 April 2027, with mining company Sibanye-Stillwater holding the naming rights to both mass participation races, which form part of an expanded festival of athletics designed to bring communities, families, aspiring athletes and elite performers together through the power of sport.

All individuals who purchase a ticket to the Simbine Classic and make a R50 donation to the Akani Simbine Foundation will automatically receive an entry into the road race. Participants who complete the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 10km in under 60 minutes will also receive a commemorative medal, while all runners and walkers will have up to 80 minutes to complete the course.

The day’s programme will feature development sprint races for emerging young athletes, competitions showcasing South Africa’s rising track and field stars, and a world-class elite programme featuring local and international athletics icons. Spectators attending the event and audiences watching from home can also look forward to a vibrant entertainment offering throughout the day. Ticket sales and entry details for the road race will be announced in the coming weeks.

“We were very pleased with the success of the 2026 Simbine Classic, and we want to go even bigger and better in 2027,” said Akani Simbine, founder of the Simbine Classic.

“The introduction of the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold road races allows us to create a platform where everyone can participate, whether they are chasing a personal best, taking their first steps into athletics, supporting a loved one, or competing on the world stage. Our vision is to make the Simbine Classic a true festival of athletics that inspires participation at every level.”

Sibanye-Stillwater’s sponsorship of the MyGold road races reflects its wider commitment to sport development, healthy lifestyles and the communities in which it operates. The partnership advances the company’s focus on inclusion and opportunity, while extending its support for youth development. As part of its commitment, the company will donate R1 million to the Akani Simbine Foundation, a non-profit organisation dedicated to empowering underserved youth through sports, education, and community welfare projects.

“The launch of the Sibanye-Stillwater MyGold 5km and 10km reinforces our commitment to creating opportunities that bring people together, promoting healthy lifestyles and inspiring the next generation of athletes. Our partnership with the Simbine Classic extends these opportunities beyond elite competition to one that encourages broad community participation and fosters social cohesion,” said Charl Keyter, Chief Financial Officer of Sibanye-Stillwater.

“Akani Simbine’s exceptional achievement in 2026 as the only athlete to run 100 metres in under 10 seconds for 12 consecutive years aligns with our own commitment to performance excellence. Our support of the Akani Simbine Foundation also complements our broader investments in education and sports development in our host communities.”

The addition of the MyGold mass participation race further strengthens the Simbine Classic’s ambition of becoming one of Africa’s premier athletics events, ensuring that the excitement and inspiration of the day can be experienced by athletes and supporters alike.
